name: Grip, Hold, Pin - Curator walkthrough
description: Join Aayati Sengupta, Curator of Grip, Hold, Pin, for a walkthrough of the exhibition. Through a close reading of the works on view, the walkthrough will explore wrestling as more than a sport—as a site where discipline, kinship, identity and everyday life converge. Drawing on photography, archival material and moving image, Grip, Hold, Pin traces the histories and lived experiences that shape wrestling cultures across India, inviting audiences to consider the relationships between body, labour, tradition and representation.

name: Grip, Hold, Pin - Deaf Led walkthrough
description:
Experience Grip, Hold, Pin: Wrestling in India through a Deaf-led walkthrough that invites audiences to look closely at how wrestling, wrestlers and the world of kushti have been represented through photography.

Led by Akanksha Kamble from the MAP team, this visual-first walkthrough explores the exhibition’s photographs documenting the lives, identities and expressions of wrestlers across India. The walkthrough opens up conversations around the physicality of wrestling, the spaces in which it is practised, and the people and communities that shape its traditions.

name: Goonga Pehelwan
description:
Goonga Pehelwan follows the extraordinary journey of Virender Singh, one of India’s most accomplished deaf wrestlers, as he pursues his dream of representing India at the 2016 Rio Olympics.
Born and raised in a small village in Haryana, Virender began wrestling at a young age and went on to build an exceptional career, including multiple Deaflympics and World Deaf Wrestling Championship medals. Yet, despite his achievements on the mat, he faced persistent barriers and limited recognition from India’s sporting establishment.

Moving between the wrestling arena, his village and the institutions that determine the fate of athletes like him, the film explores the battles Virender faces both inside and outside the ring. Goonga Pehelwan is a portrait of an athlete whose determination to compete at the highest level becomes a larger story about recognition, access and the struggles faced by deaf athletes in India.

Join the filmmaker, Vivek Chaudhary and Virender Singh for a conversation following the screening, as they reflect on the film and the story behind it.

name: Up, Close and Centre
description:
Ever wondered how wrestling was depicted before photography—and what these early images can tell us about the way we have understood sport, strength and the body?

Join Shubhashree from MAP’s Education Department as she explores depictions of women wrestling in the Raagmala paintings featured in Grip, Hold, Pin. Looking closely at these early works, the walkthrough will consider how wrestling has long existed beyond the mat—as part of India’s visual and cultural traditions—and how ideas of gender, strength, movement and identity have been represented through art across time.

name: Photography in Medias-Res
description:
How do photographs shape the ways we remember, understand and narrate history? Inspired by Grip, Hold, Pin, this workshop with Managing Editor of TAKE on Art  Dilpreet Bhullar explores the art of writing about photography.

Through close readings, discussions and writing exercises, participants will consider how photographs construct meaning, and what they reveal or leave unsaid about memory, identity and history. Moving between exhibition reviews, critical essays and personal responses, the workshop invites participants to slow down, look closely and develop new ways of writing about images.

Participants are required to bring a personal photograph or an object of their choice as a starting point for reflection and writing.

name: Invisible Inks
description:
In the second edition of Shared Futures, a talk series in conjunction with the exhibition, Beneath the Turning Sky, we take a close look into visual artist Rai’s practice and the different ways her work develops—allowing things to grow and shift along the way, with play, chance and frugality playing an important role in the process.

In conversation with curator Priya Chauhan, she will also touch on the suggestive interactions that are often present of her installations, and the ways these can shape an encounter with the work. Search Party, a video work that forms a pair with the painting that is part of the exhibition will also be screened.
The session will be followed by a hands-on workshop exploring invisible inks and ideas around latency.
Beneath the Turning Sky brings together artists working across painting, sculpture, photography, and textile practices, illuminating contemporary debates around ecology, technology, development, and our relationship with the environment. Through distinct visual languages, the exhibition asks: How might art reshape our collective stewardship of the planet?

Extending these questions beyond the gallery, Shared Futures creates a space for exchange through lectures, conversations, workshops, and other experimental formats. Across these encounters, the series considers what the arts can offer in turbulent times and how creative practices can help forge new ways of thinking, being, and building solidarity.

This series is supported by Rohini Nilekani Philanthropies Foundation
